chunks: Had they come to believe instead, and taken heed for themselves, they would surely have earned from God a far better reward. If only they had sense!
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for belief and piety according to Surah Al-Baqarah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a conditional promise where the 'reward' (mathūbah) refers to both worldly tranquility and eternal bliss, contingent upon the sincerity of the People of the Book. It highlights the concept of 'taqwa' not merely as fear, but as a comprehensive consciousness that aligns one's actions with divine will, a theme central to Imam Ali's teachings in Nahj al-Balagha. The verse serves as a critique of superficial adherence to scripture without internalizing its spiritual essence.
